title: Cajun Crawfish-Style Étouffée Gravy
description: A copper-colored roux makes a peppery Louisiana gravy for spooning over shrimp or rice.

steps.title: Start the sauce
steps.text: Warm {oil} in the 10-inch HexClad skillet over low heat.

steps.title: Toast the roux
steps.text: Stir {ap} into the oil for 6–9 minutes to an even copper color.

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Stir in {bell}, {garlic}, {paprika}, {thyme} for 2 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Simmer the base
steps.text: Whisk in {broth}, {paste}, {salt} gradually. Simmer gently for 5–7 minutes until the flavors come together.

steps.title: Smooth the base
steps.text: Cool just off the boil. Tilt the pan and blend with a submerged immersion blender until smooth.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Fold in {parsley} off heat. Measure into a heatproof jug; add hot water to reach 1 cup, or simmer excess away before serving.

notes: Yield: 1 cup. Low-sodium option for the full batch: reduce fine table salt to 0.2 g and keep the same final yield. Use unsalted broth throughout. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, use half the pepper or chile if present and thin each portion with warm water. Make ahead: chill in small jars for up to 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes, freeze in quarter-cup portions up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: whisk over low heat to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat as above. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 41 kcal, 1.1 g protein, 3.6 g total carbohydrate, 2.6 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 107 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 41 kcal, 1.1 g protein, 3.6 g total carbohydrate, 2.6 g fat, 0.5 g fiber, 29 mg sodium.
